key_insight: A mixed-primal FEM couples fourth-order solvent electrostatics with a second-order solute model while supporting accurate Maxwell stress recovery.
engineering_relevance: The method supports electrostatic stress and interaction-force calculations in ionic solutions with material interfaces.
method: Introduce auxiliary gradient and divergence fields to reformulate the fourth-order solvent equation.
Retain a primal solute formulation, avoiding Lagrange multipliers for transmission conditions.
Discretise vector fields with Raviart–Thomas elements and scalar fields with piecewise polynomials.
evidence_signal: Theoretical stability and error estimates are supported by 2D and 3D numerical experiments validating convergence rates.
watch_item: Unresolved parameter-dependent length scales can reduce convergence by up to half an order; lowest-order 3D Maxwell stress recovery is also an exception to optimal convergence.
paper_title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
